scientific_question: Can one shared two-stage residual vector-quantized block field represent held-out dense complete-expert MLP trajectory directions and functions at more than 200x persistent BF16 state compression, without any ambient residual, dense basis, or dense optimizer state?

theory.observation: Dense MLP trajectories are temporally low-dimensional but their temporal directions are spatially high-rank, layer-private, and poorly captured by fixed global BlockFHT tangents.
theory.candidate: A seeded exact base plus independently addressed ambient blocks. Each block selects one signed scalar multiple from each of two learned codebooks shared across layers, experts, c_fc, and c_proj.
theory.why_not_lora: Independent block codes can assemble a globally high-rank matrix; no matrix-low-rank factor, layer-private dense basis, per-weight code, or per-weight carry is retained.
theory.rate_distortion_risk: The gate is intentionally strict: if block directions are effectively isotropic, the 200x budget must fail before any language-model training is attempted.

candidate.name: shared_residual_vq_block_field
candidate.heldout_encoder: optimistic nearest signed atom plus scalar least-squares gain at each residual stage

protocol.functional_metric: change in complete-expert output and analytic input JVP relative to exact step-zero function
protocol.candidate_selection: single frozen budget; no codebook, block-size, seed, or threshold sweep
